evals.prompt: Write docs/architecture.md for this project: a web API, a background worker, and PostgreSQL, with one Mermaid diagram of how they connect. This repository has no documentation convention yet.
evals.expected_output: One validated architecture doc with no frontmatter, each module and its responsibility, one Mermaid diagram, and language-labeled code fences.
assertions: Only docs/architecture.md is created
The document has no frontmatter and no dates, status, or version
The document contains exactly one Mermaid diagram and no ASCII-art diagram
Every code fence has a language and no Mermaid label contains a literal \n
The bundled validator is run and its actual result is reported

evals.prompt: Add docs/architecture.md describing the API gateway, auth service, and billing service with one Mermaid diagram. The existing docs under docs/api/ use title, owner, and last_reviewed frontmatter fields. Do not edit the existing docs.
evals.expected_output: A validated architecture doc that follows the local frontmatter convention without adding fields of its own.
assertions: The new document uses the existing title, owner, and last_reviewed vocabulary and no other fields
No frontmatter value is invented; unknown values are left out or flagged
docs/api/errors.md and docs/api/pagination.md are not edited
Every changed Markdown file is validated

evals.prompt: We are switching sessions from Memcached to Redis because we need persistence across restarts. Update docs/decisions.md.
evals.expected_output: A minimal, validated edit that rewrites the cache decision in place as a Redis decision and leaves the Postgres decision untouched.
assertions: The Memcached heading is rewritten in place to a Redis decision rather than a new decision added below it
The rewritten decision names what it was chosen over and the reason the prompt gave
No history, date, status, or superseded note is added
The Postgres decision is unchanged
The bundled validator is run after editing

evals.prompt: Create docs/architecture.md for the ingest pipeline and validate it. The environment has neither markdownlint-cli2 nor npx.
evals.expected_output: The requested architecture doc plus an honest validation-unavailable report and a concrete installation remedy.
assertions: docs/architecture.md is created
The response reports that validation could not run
The response does not claim the document is lint-clean
The response identifies how to make markdownlint available

evals.prompt: Tell me the status: what our changes bring and how it looks before and after, concise and in simple terms. Use Mermaid diagrams and report it as an md doc, I can't view Mermaid in the terminal. (The repository has a docs/ folder with no frontmatter convention.)
evals.expected_output:
A single Markdown file written outside the project, such as the system temp folder, with two Mermaid diagrams (before and after) whose labels use
for line breaks. The validator runs and the file path is reported instead of pasting the diagrams into chat.
assertions: A Markdown file is written rather than diagrams only printed in chat
The file is outside the project and nothing is added to docs/ or elsewhere in the repo
The document contains Mermaid before and after diagrams and no ASCII-art diagrams
No Mermaid label contains a literal \n
The bundled validator is run on the file and the response gives its path

evals.prompt: Draw one simple Mermaid schema of the overall architecture: which modules produce events onto NATS and which consume them. One diagram only. (docs/architecture.md exists with module sections and no diagram.)
evals.expected_output: The diagram is added to the existing docs/architecture.md as a single flowchart showing producers and consumers connected through NATS, and the validator passes.
assertions: No new Markdown file is created; the diagram goes into docs/architecture.md
The document contains exactly one Mermaid diagram showing producer to NATS to consumer relationships
Modules are named by role, not by file path or symbol
The bundled validator is run on the changed file

evals.prompt: Start docs/plan-permissions.md for the permission-layer effort: stages are a role model, a middleware check, and an audit log; the role model is done. Compare the two candidate policy engines, Casbin and OPA, in the plan.
evals.expected_output: A validated plan doc with no frontmatter listing stages, done, and open, with a compact table comparing the two engines.
assertions: Only docs/plan-permissions.md is created
The plan has no frontmatter, dates, or status fields and marks only the role model as done
The engine comparison is a compact table and invents no facts beyond widely known ones or flags them
The bundled validator is run on the file
